newsitem.title: USA: Marks Bros, other retailers down on new estimates.
newsitem.headline: Marks Bros, other retailers down on new estimates.

text.p: Stocks of several high-end retail chains were down sharply Monday in the wake of several revisions of earnings and sales estimates, analysts said.

"That's just the herd mentality (on Wall Street)," explained Howard Eilenberg, an analyst at Redbook Research. "Investors say 'Let's bail out of the high-end retailer sector because one of them is having lower sales.'"
Hardest hit was Marks Brothers Jewelers Inc, which fell 37 percent after Montgomery Securities Inc lowered its fourth-quarter estimate to $0.57 a share from $0.66.
Retail analysts said Friday's announcement by Nordstrom Inc that holiday season sales would not meet expectations affected other retail stocks Monday, including Saks Holdings Inc and Gucci Group NV.
Montgomery analyst Tom Tashjian said comparable sales for December for Marks Brothers could be lower than originally planned, and inventories will be higher.
Marks Brothers officials were unavailable to comment on the stock activity, although a manager at one of the company's stores in Chicago said sales were solid, even after Chistmas.

When asked about the drop among high-end retail stocks, Karen Sack, an analyst at Standard & Poor's Ratings Services, replied "You mean the 'Nordstrom Effect?' It (the lower estimate) was a real surprise. Everyone was expecting better numbers for same-store sales."
Alan Rifkin, a retail analyst at Dain Bosworth, said the declines were not necessaarily directly related to the Nordstrom announcement.

"A lot of investors realized some solid gains in the Christmas season," he explained, "and we may be seeing some profit taking today or some window dressing before the end of the calendar year. You've got to remember that these retailers had a strong Christmas and a strong 1996."
Marks Brothers shares were down 8-1/2 Monday afternoon at 13, Saks Holdings was off 2-7/8 at 26-3/8, Gucci Group was down 2-3/8 at 65-5/8 and Nordstrom was off 1-1/2 at 36.
